understanding.heading: What Are Composite Fillings??
understanding.intro: Composite fillings are a modern solution for treating cavities and repairing minor tooth damage. Made from a strong, tooth-colored resin, they’re custom-matched to your natural enamel and bonded directly to the tooth for a seamless, long-lasting result.

process.heading: What to Expect: Our Composite Filling Process
process.intro: At Valencia Dentistry, we keep the process simple and focused on what matters—your comfort and your health. Our composite fillings are placed using modern tools and techniques that help us work efficiently while making sure you feel at ease from start to finish.

steps.title: Evaluation and Tooth Prep
steps.text: We begin with a full dental exam and digital imaging to pinpoint the affected area. Once confirmed, we gently numb the tooth and remove any decay while preserving healthy structure.

steps.title: Filling Placement
steps.text: A tooth-colored composite resin is layered and shaped to match the natural contours of your tooth for a seamless fit and feel.

steps.title: Curing, Polishing, and Bite Check
steps.text: The filling is hardened with a special curing light, polished for a smooth finish, and adjusted to ensure your bite feels completely natural.

candidate.heading: Who’s a Good Candidate for Composite Fillings?
bullets: Patients with cavities or minor tooth decay
Individuals with chipped, cracked, or worn teeth
Anyone seeking to replace old metal (amalgam) fillings
People who grind their teeth and need reinforcement
Adults and teens looking for natural-looking dental repairs
Custom-shaded to match your natural tooth color
With proper care, composite fillings can last many years
No mercury or risk of metal sensitivity
Bonds tightly to prevent future decay and damage

extra.heading: How to Care for Your Composite Fillings
paragraphs: Composite fillings are strong and built to last, but a little care goes a long way in keeping them in great shape. Just like your natural teeth, they need regular maintenance to stay clean, comfortable, and cavity-free.
bullets: Brush twice a day with a soft-bristled toothbrush and fluoride toothpaste
Floss daily to remove plaque between teeth and along the gumline
Avoid biting hard objects like ice, pens, or fingernails
Limit stain-causing foods and drinks, especially right after treatment
Schedule regular checkups and cleanings so we can monitor the filling over time
Let us know if you notice any changes like sensitivity or rough edges

faqs.q: How long do composite fillings last?
faqs.a: With proper care and regular dental visits, composite fillings can last anywhere from 5 to 10 years—or even longer. Their longevity depends on factors like the location of the filling, your oral hygiene habits, and whether you grind your teeth.

Yes. Composite fillings are metal-free and made from a durable resin material that’s safe, biocompatible, and mercury-free. They’re a great choice for patients looking for a more natural and health-conscious option.

Absolutely. One of the biggest advantages of composite fillings is their ability to match the color and texture of your natural teeth. Most people won’t even be able to tell you’ve had dental work done.

faqs.q: Will my tooth be sensitive after the procedure?
faqs.a: Some patients experience mild sensitivity for a few days after receiving a filling. This usually fades quickly. If it lasts longer or becomes uncomfortable, let us know—we’re here to help.

faqs.q: Can I eat right after getting a composite filling?
faqs.a: Since composite resin hardens immediately with a curing light, you can typically eat right after your appointment. We do recommend waiting until the numbness wears off to avoid accidentally biting your cheek or tongue.

faqs.q: How do composite fillings compare to other types?
faqs.a: Composite fillings are preferred for their aesthetic and functional benefits. Unlike silver amalgam, they bond directly to the tooth and require less drilling. You can read more about how they work and what to expect in this overview from Healthline.
